newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was rather lethargic, generally steady on fairly light demand and light to moderate offerings, compared with last week, USDA said. Retail interest was light for immediate needs and also continued light on forward interest.
Processors struggled all week keeping inventories current, trying to improve cut-out values, and controlling slaughter numbers to meet the light consumer demands.
Chuck and round cuts generally steady, but weaker undertones were noted as the week progressed.

Loin cuts were uneven during the week. Select loin cuts showed firmness late in the week, while most Choice cuts were under pressure, and the Choice tenderloins continued to trade lower. Rib cuts were generally steady during the week on both the Choice and Select cuts.

Closely trimmed items were generally steady, but demand was rather light. Beef trimmings were higher on light to moderate demand and offerings. Fed cattle and blended grinds were generally steady on light demand.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal generally steady; Select and Choice chuck primal steady to to 1.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal generally steady; Select and Choice loin primal steady to 2.00 lower; Closely trimmed items generally steady; Beef trimmings 2.50 higher; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items steady to 2.00 lower.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn $0.52 at $96.87; 700/850 Dn $0.36 at $95.46; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn $0.61 at $92.95; 700/850 Up $0.20 at $91.83.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT - Slaughter cow buyers continued to seek limited supplies of cows at higher live prices in many areas. In return they attempted to sell lean boneless beef steady to higher. Consequently, demand remained very light and buyers reduced production, resulting in declining price levels for lean boneless beef in the Midwest.

However, in the Texas market lean boneless beef traded firm due to very light offerings. Additionally, many cow cuts moved at higher price levels on light offerings and moderate demand. The 100 percent lean items continued to make price gains as seasonal demand remained moderate to fairly strong.

Utility no recent test for comparison; Cutter carcasses generally steady to firm; 90% boneless beef 1.00 lower in the Midwest, but Texas 1.00 higher; 85% steady to 2.00 lower; 75% steady; 65% steady to firm. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, February 6, 1997 was estimated at $68.96 per cwt., down $0.75 from a week ago Friday.
